study type: Retrospective cohort analysis within a sentinel surveillance network
exposure: Medication for opioid use disorder (MOUD) type (methadone, buprenorphine with naloxone, naltrexone)
outcome: Patterns of MOUD use during pregnancy (overall frequency, type distribution, timing of initiation, continuity across trimesters)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 3911 pregnancies with documented medication for opioid use disorder from January 2014 to August 2021, involving pregnant people with opioid use disorder receiving care at seven US clinical sites within the MAT-LINK network.
finding: The overall frequency of MOUD improved over the course of pregnancy, with contextual factors such as insurance status and year of pregnancy outcome influencing MOUD type.
